events.title: Sumerian City-States
events.description: The first known city-states emerge in Sumer in southern Mesopotamia, including Uruk, Ur, and Eridu. Uruk becomes the world's first major city with up to 40,000 inhabitants.

events.title: Invention of Cuneiform Writing
events.description: The Sumerians develop cuneiform, one of the world's earliest writing systems, originally used to keep records of trade and inventory.

events.title: Unification of Egypt
events.description: Narmer (Menes) unites Upper and Lower Egypt and establishes the first dynasty. Egypt becomes a unified state with its capital at Memphis.

events.title: Egyptian Hieroglyphs
events.description: The Egyptian writing system develops, using hieroglyphs on monuments and religious texts.

events.title: Indus Valley Civilization
events.description: The Harappa and Mohenjo-daro civilizations flourish in the Indus Valley with advanced urban planning, sewage systems, and trade.

events.title: The Bronze Age begins
events.description: An alloy of copper and tin produces bronze, revolutionizing tools, weapons, and technology across the ancient world.

events.title: The Old Kingdom in Egypt
events.description: Egypt enters its first golden age. Centralized royal power with the pharaoh as a divine ruler.

events.title: The Great Pyramid of Giza
events.description: The Great Pyramid is built under Pharaoh Khufu. It stands 146 meters tall and remains the world's tallest structure for over 3,800 years.

events.title: The Akkadian Empire
events.description: Sargon of Akkad establishes the world's first great empire, stretching from the Persian Gulf to the Mediterranean Sea.

events.title: Third Dynasty of Ur
events.description: Ur-Nammu founds the third dynasty in Ur and writes the world's oldest known law code, the Laws of Ur-Nammu.

events.title: Stonehenge is built
events.description: The monument Stonehenge in England takes shape with its large stone blocks. Its purpose remains debated but is likely linked to religious rituals and astronomy.

events.title: Chinese civilization along the Yellow River
events.description: Early farming communities along the Yellow River (Huang He) lay the foundation for Chinese civilization.

events.title: The Epic of Gilgamesh
events.description: The story of King Gilgamesh of Uruk is recorded, including a flood narrative with clear parallels to the biblical account of the Great Flood.
